modern: When you are troubled about anything, you have forgotten this, that all things happen according to the universal nature; and forgotten this, that a man’s wrongful act is nothing to you; and further you have forgotten this, that everything which happens always happened so and will happen so, and now happens so everywhere; forgotten this too, how close the kinship is between a man and the whole human race, for it is a community not of a little blood or seed, but of intelligence. And you have forgotten this too, that every man’s intelligence is a god and flows out from the Deity; and forgotten this, that nothing is a man’s own, but that his child and his body and his very soul came from the Deity; forgotten this, that everything is opinion; and lastly you have forgotten that every man lives only the present moment, and loses only this.

explained.summary:
Whenever you’re upset, you’ve forgotten something. Everything happens according to the way the universe works. Another person’s wrongdoing is their business, not a harm to you. Things have always happened like this and always will. You’re closely related to every human being, not by blood but by sharing in reason.

You’ve also forgotten that each person’s mind comes from the divine, that nothing, not even your child, body or soul, is truly owned, that so much rests on opinion, and that you only ever live, and only ever lose, the present moment.
explained.today: After a row with a sibling or a stinging comment from your boss, run down Marcus’s list. Usually you’ll find you’ve forgotten at least one thing, perhaps that their behaviour is theirs to answer for, or that you’re only losing this moment if you keep chewing it over.
